subject: hoverPickup
pitch:
Category: Vehicle.
Subject: militarized pickup converted to hover thrusters.
Style: low-poly cyberpunk.
reasoning:
I'm planning a single TS module for a hover pickup vehicle design—no wheels, four hover thruster pods, armored body, turret, neon underglow, and decal textures—aiming for a moderately sized, API-correct build using the part/loft/extrude/lathe/rod/sweep/glow/svg/paint functions.

I'm sketching the skeleton: chassis root, four hover thruster joints with spinning fans, turret yaw/pitch, and dimensions for a 5.2 length by 2.1 width body floating above the ground with pods touching y=0. I'm working out the hull as a lofted shape from rear to front station widths/heights, with custom paint for panelling instead of relying on kit presets, plus a tilted cab with dark teal glass built from frustum box shapes.

Now I'm shaping the hood as another tapering frustum, a bed with roll bar tubes and a yaw/pitch turret carrying twin glowing barrels, and defining the hover pods as lathed bell-shaped pods using a radius/height profile so their bases sit right at ground level.

Adding glowing cyan discs beneath each pod, tucked just inside the base so they peek out without clipping, then capping each pod with a torus ring and a six-bladed fan on a spinning joint, connected by small struts.

Now I'm positioning the fan assembly relative to the chassis, parenting the pod's spin joint to point straight up, and adding underglow light strips beneath the hull along with magenta neon trim lines down the sides. I'm also planning decal planes on the doors for text like "NOMAD-7" plus hazard stripes and an emblem, mapping textured planes onto the side faces so they align correctly with the body.

Still calculating hull width and decal placement...

Now I'm designing angular armor fenders over the hover pods, extruding a wedge-shaped outline along the side at each pod location, and checking that the pod radius and stance width overlap sensibly with the hull.

Switching to simple boxes for the fenders instead, positioned above the fan pods so they clear the fan blade height without needing a separate blade cover.

Now I'm adding details: a hood scoop, front light bar glowing magenta, headlight slits in yellow-cyan, a roof lightbar and antenna, plus rear booster thrusters with a lathed glow effect. I'm also planning hazard-striped armor plates on the bed sides, cannon barrels, and maybe roof-mounted rocket pods made from boxes with tube ends. For the body paint I'm defining a countershaded navy base run through a panelled material function with rivets, making sure panelled accepts a general color input so it composes with the paint helper.

I'm also setting up a custom dirt/grime paint using noise and smoothstep to mix a darker muddy brown into the lower parts of the body based on height and some noise variation, then wrapping that into the panelled finish. I'm defining a helper box function and planning out the part signature for placing geometry with color, position, bone, and rotation.

Now I'm working through the turret mechanics: a yaw joint positioned near the rear with a pitch joint above it, then placing the ring, drum, and barrels. I'm calculating the bed span and adjusting barrel length so they don't collide with the cab, shortening them to fit between the turret pivot and the forward edge.

With no wheels, I'm treating the thrusters as a hinge joint role. For details, I'm planning glowing headlight boxes, a side decal with "NOMAD-7" text, hazard stripes, and a skull emblem as an SVG texture on a plane, plus a glowing rear kanji sign for extra flair.

Positioning the fan blades and pod joints...
